correctness.rationale: At each cut a different sampled coordinate wraps to become least; the n ordinal permutations are distinct cyclic shifts, with probabilities equal to the circular gap lengths. Thus the defect is the relative entropy from the uniform law on n gaps. In q=q_k through Q−1, Q=q_{k+1}, the first q points lie within 1/Q of a permuted q-grid, so the largest gap is at most 1/q+2/Q, and inserting points only lowers it. This yields Δ≤log(3n/q)≤log(3(a_{k+1}+1)), including the claimed uniform bound by choosing the surrounding denominators. For a=a_{k+1}≥16, b=floor(a/log a) gives n=bq<Q. Writing an index as r+sq puts its b translates of each base point along one direction of the circle, spaced by δ=|qα−p_k|<1/Q. The arc length (b−1)δ is less than 1/(q log a), smaller than the separation of the q base points. There are exactly q large-group gaps and q(b−1) within-cluster gaps, the latter of total mass ε<1/log a. The chain rule gives H_{bq}≤log q+h(ε)+ε log(b−1), so M_k≥log a−log log a−1−o(1) uniformly in earlier quotients. Together these bounds give both the classification and the leading coefficient. For a_j=j, q_j≥j! and q_{j+1}/q_j≤j+2 imply irrationality exponent two by the convergent formula; in fact the uniform block upper bound directly gives Δ/log n→0 there. The optional finite checks are not used to establish the all-slope statement.
residual_risks: The leading coefficient is proved as a_{k+1}→∞, not a second-order expansion or order-one constant. The observation, sampling and phase measure are fixed by the theorem.

value.rationale: The additive defect measures loss of near-uniformity of ordinal patterns on a scale where the standard normalized laws discard the difference. The theorem separates bounded-type rotations from exponent-two rotations with slowly growing unbounded partial quotients and quantifies by how much at their worst phases of observation length. The uniform dependence on the current partial quotient, rather than on the whole scale q, is the useful feature.
residual_risks: No claim of a full second-order profile or extension to general observables, alternative phase laws, or noisy sampling.
